request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

membershipTier becomes 'GOLD' when the owner's household (owners sharing the same householdId) has 3 or more members after this create; otherwise the existing BRONZE and SILVER rules apply.

agent.result_text:
Tests pass. Both findings addressed:

**Finding 1 (O(N²) full-table scan per owner) — fixed.** The collection paths (`findAllOwners`, `findOwners`, `findOwnerByLastName`) no longer call `countHouseholdMembers` once per element. `decorateWithHouseholdMemberCount` now does a single `ownerRepository.findAll()`, groups it into a `householdId → count` map once, then stamps each owner from that map in O(page) time. So rendering a page of N owners is one table scan plus an O(N) assignment, not N scans.

**Finding 2 (population call scattered across five methods) — fixed.** All owner-returning paths now funnel through one helper. The single-owner overload (`findOwnerById`, `saveOwner`) delegates to the same collection-based implementation by wrapping the owner in a one-element list (and short-circuits to an empty list when the owner is `null`), so the counting logic lives in exactly one place. A future read method that forgets to decorate still won't get a compile-time signal — that's inherent to it being a cross-cutting runtime concern (and, as the review notes, `@PostLoad` can't own this since the count depends on sibling rows) — but the concern is now a single, named, reusable funnel rather than copy-pasted `forEach` lines.

I kept the mapper, `Owner` transient field, Javadoc, and OpenAPI changes as-is, since the review found them clean. Acceptance behaviour is unchanged: `coreGoldForThreeMemberHousehold` still passes (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 1 test, 0 failures).

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The transient-field + service-populate + mapper-read split is a reasonable fit for how this service already derives read-only fields (it mirrors the `countNamesakes` / `countOwnersInCity` / `countRegisteredToday` helper family, and `countHouseholdMembers` slots in idiomatically next to them). But two structural issues are worth fixing before this reads as natural to a maintainer:

1. **Per-owner full-table scan inside the collection loops (O(N²)).** `countHouseholdMembers` calls `ownerRepository.findAll()` and filters in memory, and `populateHouseholdMemberCount` is invoked once per owner via `owners.forEach(...)` in `findAllOwners`, `findOwners`, and `findOwnerByLastName`. So rendering a page of N owners re-reads the entire owner table N times. The existing `countX` helpers are only ever called once per create, so this is a *new* pattern, not an established one. For the collection paths the household sizes should be computed in a single pass — e.g. load all owners once, group by `householdId`, then assign each owner its group size — rather than a fresh `findAll()` per element. The single-owner paths (`findOwnerById`, `saveOwner`) can keep the simple helper.

2. **The population call is manually scattered across five methods.** Every read/save path has to remember to call `populateHouseholdMemberCount`, and a future read method that forgets it will silently drop GOLD with no compile-time signal. Because the count depends on sibling rows (not just the entity), a JPA `@PostLoad` on `Owner` can't cleanly own this, so the service is the right unit — but consider funneling the owner-returning paths through a single private "decorate owners before return" helper so the cross-cutting concern lives in one place instead of being copy-pasted as `owners.forEach(this::populateHouseholdMemberCount)` in four spots.

The `OwnerMapper`, `Owner` transient field, Javadoc, and OpenAPI changes themselves are clean and consistent with surrounding conventions; the concerns above are confined to `ClinicServiceImpl`.
